style.vernacular: Hillside city above the bay known as Algiers the White: the Casbah is a dense maze of whitewashed Ottoman courtyard houses with flat terraces and few windows, below it French-colonial Haussmann-style 5-6 storey apartment blocks in cream and ochre stone with wrought-iron balconies and arcaded ground floors, neo-Moorish public buildings (post office, museums), 1970s-80s concrete slab blocks and towers, and tiled villas on the hills.
style.ornament: Horseshoe and pointed arches, glazed tile panels (zellige-style) and carved plaster on neo-Moorish buildings; Ottoman marble columns and octagonal minarets; wrought-iron balconies and arcaded street fronts in the Haussmann quarters; blue-painted doors and shutters; ficus and palm avenues.

sources.what: Whitewashed city (Algiers the White); Casbah of Ottoman/Andalusian houses; French Haussmann-style apartment blocks, boulevards and Place des Martyrs
Neo-Moorish (Moorish Revival) public building, 1910
Moorish-Byzantine blend, octagonal minarets, marble columns, stone and marble
